why.org_a:finding:06850: Enables internet-exposed access to ember-basalt-edge-183, leading directly to crown jewel data via stolen SSH credentials.
why.org_a:finding:06851: Provides an entry point on cobalt-sol-edge-184 that permits local privilege escalation and subsequent database access.
why.org_a:finding:06853: Serves as an internet-facing vulnerability on fjord-basalt-edge-185 that forms part of an active attack path to crown jewels.
why.org_a:finding:06855: Exposes ember-tessera-edge-186 to the internet, allowing attackers to leverage exposed cloud credentials against storage.
why.org_a:finding:06848: Acts as the initial internet-facing vulnerability on larch-meadow-edge-182, bridging to internal database compromise.
why.org_a:finding:06856: Facilitates remote service exploitation from compromised edge assets to internal CI nodes.
why.org_a:finding:06879: Constitutes an internet-facing edge vulnerability on vireo-basalt-edge-192 participating in attack paths toward sensitive data.

reasoning: We prioritized findings that lie directly on attack paths originating from the Internet and leading to the crown jewel data store (org_a:ds:00001). Using attack path analysis and min-cut simulation, we identified the minimal set of seven internet-facing and internal vulnerabilities whose remediation completely disconnects external attacker access to the crown jewels.
